source.citation: Kendall Haven, "100 Greatest Science Discoveries of All Time", Libraries Unlimited, 2007
source.note: This file is a preliminary, unreviewed extraction of the book's table of contents. Page numbers below were read directly from the book's own contents pages and are believed accurate. Nothing else in this file, category, approximate period, or the social-adjustment question, comes from reading the book's chapter text itself. Haven's own book explicitly covers discoveries, not inventions, and excludes anything he could not attribute to one person or a small team, so most entries here describe a fact found out about nature rather than a technology, practice, or system entering a society. Only a fraction of this list is expected to become a full case in this project. Nothing here should be treated as authoritative or complete, and no page number, category, period, or question below should be cited as coming from Haven's own text until it has been checked against the book directly.
source.candidateStatusMeaning: unreviewed means the entry has not been checked against the book's chapter text, against other sources, or against this project's case-eligibility rules.
